name: North Buttress Couloir

pitch_detail.notes: From the far side of Colchuck Lake, hike up and gain the moraine, follow it right to the couloir entrance at the glacier's edge.
Climb steep snow filling the gully.
As snow thins later in the season, a few short Class 4 rock steps are exposed.
Top-out can be guarded by a cornice that has required over an hour to breach in some reported conditions.

rappels: None typical — most parties walk off via the Colchuck Glacier/Col; a short roped pitch (not a rappel) is sometimes used near the summit
descent_text: Descend the backside of the mountain onto the Colchuck Glacier and follow its standard route and the moraine back to Colchuck Lake; in soft, late-day snow this descent has been reported as slow and exhausting.
approach: Follow the shared Colchuck Peak approach: from Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road ~8.4 mi to FR 7601, then FR 7601 ~3.7 mi to Stuart Lake Trailhead; hike the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake Trail (~4-4.5 mi, ~2,200 ft gain) to Colchuck Lake. From the lake's far (south) side, hike up and gain the moraine, follow it to the right, and drop into the couloir — it is the first major gully reached rising out of the toe of the Colchuck Glacier's moraine.
overview: The most direct couloir rising out of the Colchuck Glacier's moraine on Colchuck Peak's north side — a popular introduction to steep snow and easy mixed climbing, with conditions ranging from a straightforward snow slog to thin mixed rock-and-ice.
beta: From the far side of Colchuck Lake, hike uphill to gain the moraine, follow it to the right, and drop into the large couloir at the edge of the Colchuck Glacier. In winter and early season it is continuous snow the entire way; later in summer, Class 4 rock can be exposed in a few short steps. The route can be climbed minimalist and fast, or fully protected with rock gear, pickets, and screws. Descent is via the Colchuck Glacier route on the peak's far side.
gear: Light rock rack (cams ~0.5-2 in, small pitons, nuts)
fa: Ray Lilleby and Jim Wickwire, July 1962
